Comments: The Department received a complaint on 3/5/2025 that there were E and S issues with the access road for the Samual Serian 1 1470 well. On 3/10/2025, I conducted a complaint inspection of Diversified Production, LLC's Samuel Serian 1 1470 well (API 063-33033) in Grant Twp., Indiana County. During my inspection, I observed numerous areas of accelerated erosion. Violations were cited for the erosion and sedimentation issues with the access road. A Notice of Violation was sent on 3/20/2025, and Diversified sent a response on 3/28/2025. On 4/11/2025, Brian Shank (WQSS) and I met Heather Empfield, AJ Smith and John Stibrik at the access road for the Samual Serian 1 1470 well. We discussed different ideas to address the culvert and eroding access road. Today, Brian Shank, Samantha Lutz (Aquatic Biologist 2), Danielle Zimmerman (Environmental Engineer) and I met at the access road for the Samual Serian 1 1470 well. The Department recommends submitting a GP11 to replace the culvert and repair the access road. The existing 4 culvert pipes will need to be replaced with a single pipe. The outstanding violations from the 3/10/2025 complaint inspection will remain open.

Comments: On 11/07/2024, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the POCKY F26 OG Well in Fallowfield Township, Washington County.The following was observed during inspection:-A well tag was observed on the well head (Photo 1).-The well and operator's information was displayed and visible at the well site as required by OGA 3211(g) (Photo 2).-Some corrosion was observed on the well head, pump jack and production equipment. It appears the belt from the pump jack is dry rotted. I recommend replacing it (Photos 3-7).-I observed over-range fluid built up on the well head and threads. It appears the well head is leaking (Photo 8-14).-It appears the elevate fluid is leaking from the well head to the ground below at the base of the well and adjacent to it. I observed elevated conductivity fluid in the ground around the whole well head. I received 9.21 mS/cm, 6.00 mS/cm, 7.06 mS/cm, 7.94 mS/cm, 5.35 mS/cm, 1636 uS/cm, and 304 uS/cm (Photo 15-21).-0.0 uS/cm base reading was on metal well head (Photo 22).Conductivity probe was calibrated on 11/07/2024 before inspection was conducted.Operator was contacted and notified on 11/07/2024. Diversified JR Wilson arrived on site and location of elevated readings were shown to him. Violations are being issued for: 78.54, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301.

properties.content:

Comments: Field inspection performed in afternoon with warm, sunny weather conditions and 84 degrees. Last inspection performed on 10/14/03, over 17 years ago. Wellhead located nearby, adjacent to surface equipment. At the wellhead surface casing valve is open, lower production tubular valve at head is closed, upper production tubular valve at head is open, and the production tubular plumbed to sales/surface equipment valve is open; annulus is buried below grade, could not determine if vented. (photo #1). No Well label/marker affixed to wellhead identifying well bore (photo #1). Some trace to minor corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The surface/ground production equipment and one 100 bbl steel tank contained by earthen dike (photo #2). Valves are open at production equipment with a 7-day production chart present with recorded values dated 7/5/21 (photo #3). Well posting signage affixed to steel tank (photo #4). Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit and tank. Staining present at base of steel tank near and around drain port on the ground and gravel surrounding; residual leak markings visible on side of tank (photo #5). Operator has submitted 2020 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well stating 510 psig. No pressure gauge was on wellhead during inspection. Operator has submitted annual production report (APR) for 2020 for this well stating 3,276 MCF recorded over 365 days. This is an active, producing well. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for well labeling OGA3211(H).

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Date: 4/04/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 950100
Permit API: 053-26904
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/04/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to the report of a discharge of crude oil from this well on April 2, 2022. The release occurred as a result of vandalism, in which a third party individual who had climbed the pump jack damaged a valve on the gathering lime riser when jumping off of the jack. Pennsylvania State Police investigated the incident and the responsible party was found and reportedly admitted what had happened. Upon my arrival, repairs have been made and there was no active discharge. The majority of the released product remained on the well site and a portion of the spur road leading to it. The contaminated soil/rock from the location and road (approximately 3-5 tons) has been excavated and placed on a contained pit liner for upcoming disposal. There was no evidence that any of the released product entered the road ditch that runs alongside the spur road. No watercourses were impacted as a result of this incident. Crews were in the process of removing oil soaked leaves along the edge of the road/location. After that work is completed, no additional remediation measures appear necessary, as the ground underneath the leaves does not appear to be impacted per field screening. A future inspection will be conducted to evaluate if any additional measures are necessary.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/07/2021
Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to a spill reported by the operator on 4/7/21 at approximately 11:53 AM. According to the operator, while drilling at the Bakerstown Rd Pad 8H, "a synthetic oil-based drilling mud (SOBM) was inadvertently sent to the gas buster. The SOBM flowed through the flare line, filled the eco tank and then was released from the top of the flare stack. The onsite vac unit and absorbent pads were utilized to collect standing SOBM." The following is observed: The Pioneer 76 rig is on site. Due to the nature of the incident, drilling operations have been temporarily suspended until the flare stack is back in operation. SPSI is on site conducting remediation. Material is being removed from the riprap lined pad ditch line (2, 3, 7, & 8). It appears that impacted water has gotten into the perforated drainpipe and migrated along it (7). The extent of this migration is not known; however, the outlet box is observed to be free of impacted material at this time. The operator has closed the outlet pipe to the level spreader. The Department requests that the operator notify the WQS prior to reopening the drain. In the interim, the EI stated that the outlet box will be monitored and drained using a vac truck as needed. The Department requested photographs of the extent of the excavation necessary to remediate the spill, specifically around the perforated drainpipe. The EI stated that the plan was to excavate until they reached "clean" pipe and cut away the impacted portion. The Department requests that the operator notify the WQS if this course of action needs to be modified. The Department also recommended that the flare stack either be moved away from the ditch line or have secondary containment installed. According to the EI, the site will be remediated under Act 2 requirements. The Department requests a copy of the waste manifest when it is available. The SDS sheet for the drilling mud and PPC/ERP is on-site. According to the secondary containment inspection record at the site, 4/7/21 is listed as the only inspection/incident to have occurred. The Department requests information on when the secondary containment was installed and when the most recent drilling operations began at the site. Based on this inspection, violations are being issued for the spill. Pending the operator’s response, more violations may be issued.

Comments: At time of inspection. On site for the conclusion of a 72hr shut in test as part of a MIT (mechanical integrity test). I met with Trey Sites (Lease Operator) for Chesapeake Oil & Gas. Violation ID: 8154570
Permit API: 033-23894
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Ferguson Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/07/2023
Comments: Diversified Prod LLC reported a brine spill to the Department on August 3, 2023 which occurred at conventional well 033-23894. I conducted a site inspection on August 7, 2023 and met with Diversified EHS Specialist's Paul Stiner and Will Warfel. Diversified has delineated the impacted area to be approximately 30' x 40'. They have installed E and S controls downslope of the excavation area. Diversified started excavation on August 5, 2023. Impacted soils were placed on plastic. Due to heavy rainfalls during my inspection the operator has postponed excavation. A dump truck was onsite upon my arrival and was loaded with impacted soils. Soils are being hauled offsite to Carbon Limestone Landfill in Ohio. Fluids with in the brine tank have been vacuumed out and properly disposed. According to Mr. Stiner, all fluids will be removed and the brine tank will be moved in order to excavate impacted soils. I randomly screened within the delineated impacted area with a Hanna Gro Line Soil Tester. Readings exceeded 4.0 mS/cm which is the maximum conductivity reading for this soil probe. Additional screenings were conducted outside the delineated area and the readings were not elevated. A soil sample was collected (3442694) and was sent to the Departments lab in Harrisburg to be tested for SAC 530 plus, bromide, lithium, and strontium. Diversified is planning to go through the Act 2 for site remediation. Moody Environmental has been hired to assist them for site remediation. Violations have been cited.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/23/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Johnson K 02-135 well site located in Hamilton Township, Tioga County on 2/23/2023 at 0935 hours. The weather was 37 degrees with fog. A layer of snow covered the majority of the site today. An Act 9 sign is located at the site entrance.This inspection was conducted in response to a reported release called in to the DEP by Repsol on 2/16/2023. On 2/16/2023 at 0900 hours, a release of 18.7 gallons of produced water mixed with sand was released to the pad surface and containment from a sand trap. Repsol promptly called in the release to the DEP reporting hotline and began cleanup activities. A Repsol representative provided photos of the cleanup to me via email on 2/22/2023.During today's inspection, the impacted area was observed to have been excavated. All impacted material recovered was placed into containers for later disposal. No evidence of any portion of the release remaining was observed today. Pooled water in and around the impacted area was field measured for electrical conductivity ranging from 160 to 320us/cm. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #370057 is tied to this release within CTS.Based on the reported release of 18.7 gallons of produced water to the pad surface and containment, violations of 35 P.S. 691.402(b), 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), and 35 P.S. 6018.301 are cited against API #117-22124. However, due to Repsol's timely remediation of the reported release, these violations are considered immediately corrected at this time. Violations from a previous issue cited on 8/10/2022 and 9/2/2022 remain outstanding against API #117-22124. I departed the site at 1100 hours.

Well location and facility field verified and GPS coordinates of wellhead updated with this inspection showed a distance offset of ~41 ft between coordinates (photo #10). Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.

Permit API: 047-24928
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/21/2025
Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone call made by Jeff Passerrello, of Seneca Resources, on November 21, 2025. The purpose of the phone call was to report an incident which had occurred on the E09-M well pad.It was reported that approximately 30 gallons of coolant fluid was released from a pin hole leak in a glycol line on the E09-M well pad. Approximately 10 gallons remained in secondary containment, while approximately 20 gallons spilled onto the well pad. The release was contained to approximately a 14'X12' area on the pad. Upon arrival to the site, the contaminated material on the pad had been excavated and placed within a secondary containment and covered with a large tarp. The glycol line had been repaired. A dumpster had arrived on the site for disposal of the contaminated material. The contaminated material will be tested and taken to a local landfill to be properly disposed of. It is requested that a copy of the documentation for disposal be provided to the Department. Given there is no ongoing discharge and the impacted area appears to have been sufficiently remediated, the violations associated with this incident are considered corrected. A future inspection or site visit will be conducted to ensure that the initial remediation efforts were sufficient.
